title: Otterly.ai Gemini & Claude Add-On Cost: What You Actually Pay
metaTitle: Otterly.ai Gemini & Claude Add-On Cost Explained
metaDescription: Gemini and Claude aren't included in Otterly.ai's base plans. Here's the real per-tier add-on cost and what full multi-engine coverage actually runs you.
shortAnswer: On Otterly.ai, only ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, and Microsoft Copilot are included by default. intro:
"Multi-engine AI search monitoring" is Otterly.ai's headline pitch, but the engines most people care about most — Gemini and Claude — aren't in the base price. They're add-ons stacked on top of your plan, and the cost scales with your tier.

This page lays out exactly what those add-ons cost, what "full coverage" actually totals, and how to decide whether it's worth it for your situation. We'll also be upfront about where a free tool like AEOeye fits and where it doesn't.

sections.heading: What's included vs. what costs extra
sections.body:
Otterly.ai's three self-serve tiers — Lite ($29/mo), Standard ($189/mo), and Premium ($489/mo) — all include the same four engines by default: **ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, and Microsoft Copilot**.

Three engines are *not* included and must be purchased as add-ons:

- **Google Gemini**
- **Google AI Mode**
- **Claude**

That's the important nuance. When Otterly markets broad AI-engine coverage, the version of that coverage you actually get on day one stops at four engines. Gemini (the consumer Google model many of your buyers use), Google's conversational AI Mode, and Claude all sit behind a paywall on top of whatever plan you're already paying for. None of the three is bundled at any tier — not even Premium. So the gap between the marketing story and the out-of-the-box product is real, and it widens precisely on the engines that have grown fastest in actual consumer usage.

sections.heading: The exact add-on cost per tier
sections.body:
Add-on pricing scales with your plan, so the more prompts you track, the more each extra engine costs. Here are the published monthly figures:

| Add-on | Lite | Standard | Premium |
|---|---|---|---|
| Google AI Mode | $9 | $59 | $149 |
| Google Gemini | $9 | $59 | $149 |
| Claude | $29 | $109 | $439 |

Annual billing trims roughly 15% off these, but the structure is the same: every engine you add is a separate recurring line item.

Notice Claude is the most expensive add-on at every tier — $439/month on Premium alone, more than the Premium base plan's $489. If Claude visibility matters to you (and for many B2B and research-heavy categories it does, since Claude users skew toward considered purchases), that single add-on can rival the cost of your whole subscription.

sections.heading: What 'full coverage' really totals
sections.body:
The sticker price you compare against competitors is rarely the price you pay for the complete multi-engine picture. Add it up on the Standard plan, the one Otterly marks 'Most Popular':

- Standard base: **$189**
- Google Gemini: **+$59**
- Google AI Mode: **+$59**
- Claude: **+$109**
- **Total: ~$416/month**

So a plan advertised at $189 lands north of $400 once you actually cover Gemini, Google AI Mode, and Claude. The same pattern holds at Lite ($29 base → ~$76 with all three) and Premium ($489 → ~$1,226).

This isn't hidden or dishonest — Otterly publishes every number on its pricing page. But it does mean you should budget for the all-in figure, not the headline tier, if a true cross-engine view is what you're buying the tool for. Compare apples to apples: the cost to monitor *all* the engines, not just the four that come bundled.

sections.heading: Is the add-on model actually a problem?
sections.body:
Not necessarily — it depends on what you need. The à la carte structure has a genuine upside: if you only care about ChatGPT and Perplexity, you never pay for Claude or Gemini, and the $29 Lite tier is a legitimately cheap entry point into ongoing tracking.

Otterly is also a mature, established monitoring platform. It offers continuous tracking, sentiment analysis, 50-plus country localization, GEO URL audits, and API/MCP access on higher tiers — depth that a free instant audit doesn't replicate. If you need historical dashboards, scheduled re-runs, and team workflows, that ongoing platform is doing real work for the money.

The model only becomes a problem when the marketing implies broad coverage is included and the budget reality is that it isn't. If you walked in expecting Gemini and Claude in the box, the climb from $189 to ~$416 is a fair thing to feel surprised by. Knowing the structure up front lets you decide deliberately instead of discovering it at checkout.

faqs.q: Are Gemini and Claude included in Otterly.ai's base plans?
faqs.a: No. Every Otterly tier (Lite, Standard, Premium) includes ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, and Microsoft Copilot by default. Gemini, Google AI Mode, and Claude are all separate paid add-ons at every tier, including Premium.

faqs.q: How much does the Claude add-on cost on Otterly.ai?
faqs.a: Claude costs $29/month on Lite, $109/month on Standard, and $439/month on Premium. It's the most expensive add-on engine — on Premium it costs nearly as much as the base plan itself. Annual billing reduces these by roughly 15%.

faqs.q: What does Otterly.ai really cost with all engines added?
faqs.a: On the $189/month Standard plan, adding Gemini (+$59), Google AI Mode (+$59), and Claude (+$109) brings the total to about $416/month. The headline tier price doesn't reflect full multi-engine coverage.

faqs.q: Does Otterly.ai have a free tier?
faqs.a: No. Otterly offers a free trial (no permanent free plan). If you want to check your multi-engine AI visibility for free first, AEOeye runs a free, instant audit across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude, and Gemini with no add-on fees or trial clock.

faqs.q: Is Otterly.ai's add-on pricing a dealbreaker?
faqs.a: Not for everyone. If you only need a couple of engines, the à la carte model can keep costs low, and Otterly is a mature platform with deep ongoing analytics. It's only a concern if you assumed broad coverage was included — knowing the structure up front lets you budget for the all-in figure rather than the headline tier.
